A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results indicate that a theoretical flow regime type avalanche model may be too restrictive in that it describes a limiti ng case, which does not always occur even under controlled laboratory conditions The results suggest that a model which allows for a more gradual transition from a channel flow regime to a flow regime type is required, and also that the concept of a Coulomb like yield is not necessarily appropriate for avalanches of the type investigated here.

a theoretical model based on the assumption that avalanches can be described in terms of a single flow regime is too restrictive in the sense that a limiting case of avalanche flow is described, which does not always occur even under controlled experimental conditions.

the behaviour of a non cohesive, granular medium down an inclined, curved surface is complex, and the theoretical concepts of a flow regime type model may not adequately describe the physical situation in the sense that the limiting case described is not always observed, even in the controlled conditions of the laboratory experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the behavior of granular flows is complex and not well understood, and that the behavior of the granular material depends strongly on the details of the experiment and the material.
the flow of a non-cohesive granular medium down a curved inclined surface can be characterized by the flow regime, which in turn depends upon the particle size and the bed roughness.
the flow of granular media down an inclined plane is not a simple process, and that it may be necessary to consider more than one flow regime in a model.
